verdict.rationale: Rive's docs say its runtimes are open-source libraries, and the public rive-runtime GitHub repo exposes readable runtime and renderer code. Community evidence says the MIT license covers only the rendering/runtime layer, while the Editor that creates content stays closed. So only part of the product's source is readable under an open license. Missing for 10: open source for the Editor (the core product), first-party documentation naming the specific license and its scope.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The Rive runtimes are open-source libraries that allow you to load and control your animations in apps, games, and websites.
Loads .riv files, advances state machines and animations, and draws via the abstract Renderer interface.
But this is an MIT license for Rive's rendering abstraction layer, a subset of the Rive runtime that requires the Rive Editor to build content for.
